solution: Solution: Given $f(x+y)=f(x)+12y$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$ . By swapping $x$ and $y$ , we also get $f(x+y)=f(y)+12x$ . Hence $f(x)+12y=f(y)+12x$ for all $x,y$ . solution: Solution: Numbers between $1000$ and $10000$ are exactly the four-digit numbers. The intended condition is that the digits $3$ and $7$ each occur exactly once; the other two places can be filled by any digit other than $3$ and $7$ . Case $1$ : The first digit is $3$ or $7$ . Choose it in $2$ ways. Place the other required digit in any of the remaining $3$ places: $3$ ways. Fill the last two places with any of the $8$ digits excluding $3$ and $7$ : $8 	imes 8$ ways. So this case gives $2 	imes 3 	imes 8 	imes 8 = 384$ . Case $2$ : The first digit is neither $3$ nor $7$ . It cannot be $0$ , so there are $7$ choices. Place $3$ and $7$ in two of the remaining three places: $3 	imes 2 = 6$ ways. Fill the last place with any of the $8$ digits excluding $3$ and $7$ : $8$ ways. So this case gives $7 	imes 6 	imes 8 = 336$ . Total $= 384 + 336 = 720$ . Hence the correct option is $720$ . Note: If 'without repetition' were applied to all four digits, the count would be $630$ , which is not among the given options; so the intended exam reading is the one above. © examsnet.com

Now $\frac{1}{t(t+1)}=\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{t+1}$ . Thus $I=\frac{1}{4}\left(\log|t|-\log|t+1|\right)+c=\frac{1}{4}\log\left|\frac{t}{t+1}\right|+c$ . Substitute back $t=x^4$ : $I=\frac{1}{4}\log\left(\frac{x^4}{x^4+1}\right)+c$ . Hence the correct option is $\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{x^4}{x^4+1}\right) + c$ . © examsnet.com

question: Arrange the following in the increasing order of number of unpaired electrons present in the central metal ion I. $\;\; [\mathrm{Mn}  \mathrm{Cl}_6]^{3-}$ II. $\;\; [\mathrm{FeF} 6]^{3-}$ III. $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}) 6]^{3-}$ IV. $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}$ [AP EAPCET 20 May 2024 Shift 2]

question: Which of the following amino acids possess two chiral centres? [AP EAPCET 20 May 2024 Shift 2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: The correct answer is Threonine . A chiral centre is a carbon atom bonded to four different groups. For the options given, we examine the structure of each amino acid: Leucine: $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{COOH}$ . Only the $\alpha$ -carbon is bonded to four different groups, so it has only one chiral centre. Valine: $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{COOH}$ . Here again only the $\alpha$ -carbon is chiral, so it has only one chiral centre. Serine: $\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{COOH}$ . The $\beta$ -carbon bears two identical hydrogen atoms, so it is not chiral; serine has only one chiral centre. Threonine: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{COOH}$ . Both the $\alpha$ -carbon (bonded to $\text{NH}_2$ , $\text{COOH}$ , $\text{H}$ and the side chain) and the $\beta$ -carbon (bonded to $\text{OH}$ , $\text{H}$ , $\text{CH}_3$ and the rest of the molecule) are bonded to four different groups. Therefore threonine possesses two chiral centres and hence exists as four stereoisomers ( $\text{L}$ -threonine, $\text{D}$ -threonine, $\text{L}$ -allothreonine and $\text{D}$ -allothreonine). Among the given options, only threonine has two chiral centres. © examsnet.com
